title: Normalization of the small-etale representable pullback comparison
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $P\to Y$ be an object of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Put $P'=X\times_YP$, using the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $h_P(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_Y(W,P)$ and $h_{P'}(W')=\operatorname{Mor}_X(W',P')$ for their sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets, lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. Take the inverse/direct-image adjunction on sheaves of sets [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], with $(f_*H)(W)=H(X\times_YW)$. Let $\beta:h_P\to f_*h_{P'}$ send $a:W\to P$ to the morphism $\mathrm{id}_X\times_Ya:X\times_YW\to P'$. Then its adjunct
$$c:f^{-1}h_P\longrightarrow h_{P'}$$
is an isomorphism. More precisely, for every sheaf of sets $H$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, the natural bijection
$$\Phi_H:\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}h_P,H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(h_{P'},H)$$
obtained by the adjunction and evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_P$ followed by inverse Yoneda evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_{P'}$ satisfies $\Phi_{h_{P'}}(c)=\mathrm{id}_{h_{P'}}$. Equivalently $c$ is the unique morphism whose adjunct evaluated at $\mathrm{id}_P$ is $\mathrm{id}_{P'}\in h_{P'}(P')$. The comparisons $c$ are natural in $Y$-morphisms between objects $P$ of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$.

proof.text: The functor $b_f:Y_{\mathrm{et}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$, $W\mapsto X\times_YW$, is defined on every object and sends an arrow $a$ to $\mathrm{id}_X\times_Ya$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. In particular $P'=b_f(P)$ is etale over $X$. Both $h_P$ and $h_{P'}$ are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. The maps $\beta_W(a)=b_f(a)$ form a natural transformation: for $r:W_1\to W$ and $a:W\to P$, functoriality gives $\beta_{W_1}(a\circ r)=b_f(a)\circ b_f(r)$, exactly the restriction of $\beta_W(a)$ in $f_*h_{P'}$.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (4), displayed adjunction/Yoneda proof; objects and representable sheaves in the displayed proof

proof.text:
Set $A=f^{-1}h_P$ and $B=h_{P'}$. For every sheaf $H$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, let $\operatorname{adj}_H:\operatorname{Hom}(A,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(h_P,f_*H)$ be the adjunction bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], clause (1). Sheaf morphisms are exactly presheaf natural transformations by [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Thus [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], first on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ at $P$ and then on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ at $P'$, gives bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A,H)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{adj}_H}\operatorname{Hom}(h_P,f_*H)\xrightarrow{\tau\mapsto\tau_P(\mathrm{id}_P)}(f_*H)(P)=H(P')\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_{P'}^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}(B,H).$$
Call the composite $\Phi_H$. Each arrow is natural in $H$: this is adjunction naturality, the presheaf-variable naturality in the cited Yoneda statement, and the defining equality for $f_*$. Hence $\Phi$ is a natural family of bijections.

proof.text:
Take $c=\operatorname{adj}_{B}^{-1}(\beta)$. By Step 1 and functoriality,
$$\operatorname{adj}_{B}(c)_P(\mathrm{id}_P)=\beta_P(\mathrm{id}_P)=b_f(\mathrm{id}_P)=\mathrm{id}_{P'}.$$
Yoneda evaluation sends $\mathrm{id}_B$ to the same section $\mathrm{id}_{P'}\in B(P')$, so its injectivity [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] gives $\Phi_B(c)=\mathrm{id}_B$. Moreover the composite of the adjunction bijection [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] with evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_P$ is injective. Consequently $c$ is the unique morphism $A\to B$ with the displayed adjunct value. This proves both normalization formulations for the specified map, rather than choosing an unrelated isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] in the category of sheaves of sets on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ to Step 2. It gives an isomorphism $\theta=\Phi_A(\mathrm{id}_A):B\to A$ satisfying $\Phi_H(u)=u\circ\theta$ for all $u:A\to H$. At $H=B$ and $u=c$, Step 3 therefore says $c\circ\theta=\mathrm{id}_B$. Composing this equality on the right with $\theta^{-1}$ gives $c=\theta^{-1}$, so the normalized comparison $c$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (4), displayed adjunction/Yoneda proof; conclusion from the natural Hom-bijection; Categories Tag 001P on the opposite category

proof.text:
Let $t:P\to Q$ be a morphism in $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, set $t_X=b_f(t):P'\to Q'$, and write $h_t,h_{t_X}$ for postcomposition. For every $a:W\to P$, functoriality in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] gives
$$((f_*h_{t_X})\circ\beta^P)_W(a)=t_X\circ b_f(a)=b_f(t\circ a)=(\beta^Q\circ h_t)_W(a).$$
Thus $(f_*h_{t_X})\circ\beta^P=\beta^Q\circ h_t$. Under the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], naturality in its target takes the left side to $h_{t_X}\circ c_P$, and naturality in its source takes the right side to $c_Q\circ f^{-1}(h_t)$. The adjunction bijection is injective, so these two morphisms agree. This is precisely naturality of the comparisons in $P$.
